voter_id.t: No photo ID to vote; signature checks and other methods are enough.
yes: Voting with signature checks or non-photo ID

voter_id.t: Photo ID, but with many accepted IDs, free IDs and a backup option for people without one.
yes: Broad ID lists, free IDs and sworn statements as backup

voter_id.t: Photo ID, with free IDs for anyone, but no backup option.
yes: Required photo ID with free IDs
no: Backup options for people without ID

voter_id.t: Government-issued photo ID with no backup option.
yes: Strict government photo ID to vote
no: Student IDs, backups or signature checks instead

proof_of_citizenship.t: A sworn statement and existing checks are enough proof of citizenship to register.
Require citizenship documents only when government records can't confirm it.
yes: Document checks when records fall short

proof_of_citizenship.t: Everyone registering should show a passport, birth certificate or similar document.
yes: Documentary proof of citizenship for every registrant

mail_voting.t: Every voter should get a mail ballot automatically.
yes: All-mail elections, as in Colorado and Washington

mail_voting.t: Any voter who asks should be able to vote by mail.
Only voters with a reason, like illness or travel, should vote by mail.
Almost no one should vote by mail; vote in person.

mail_ballot_deadline.t: Count mail ballots postmarked by Election Day that arrive within a week or more.
yes: A grace period of a week or longer

mail_ballot_deadline.t: Count postmarked mail ballots that arrive within 3 days.
Count only mail ballots received by Election Day.

auto_registration.t: Register eligible citizens automatically at agencies like the DMV, unless they opt out.
no: Requiring people to sign up themselves

auto_registration.t: Offer registration at agencies, but people must choose to sign up.
People should register to vote on their own.

felony_voting.t: People with felony convictions should always be able to vote, even in prison.
yes: Voting from prison, as in Maine and Vermont
no: Taking away voting rights for felonies

felony_voting.t: People with felony convictions should vote once released from prison.
People with felony convictions should vote after finishing parole or probation.
yes: Restoring the vote after the full sentence

felony_voting.t: Voting rights only after a waiting period or individual review.
People convicted of a felony should never vote again.

electoral_college.t: Elect the president by national popular vote, ending the Electoral College.
Keep the Electoral College, but split each state's votes by its vote share.
Keep the Electoral College as it is.

popular_vote_loser.t: Winning the presidency while losing the national vote should be impossible.
yes: Changing the system so the vote winner always wins

popular_vote_loser.t: It's acceptable, but the system should change to make it rarer.
yes: Reforms that make it less likely

popular_vote_loser.t: It's acceptable; it reflects the role of states in choosing the president.
no: Changing the system to prevent it

redistricting.t: Independent commissions with no politicians should draw congressional districts.
Commissions with equal members from both parties should draw districts.
State legislatures should draw districts once every 10 years after the census.
State legislatures should draw districts whenever they choose, including mid-decade.
yes: Mid-decade redistricting by legislatures, for either party
no: Limits on when maps are redrawn

campaign_spending.t: Strict limits on election spending by corporations, unions and the wealthy, with a constitutional amendment if needed.
No spending limits, but full disclosure of who pays for political ads.
yes: Disclosure of donors behind political ads

campaign_spending.t: No limits or disclosure rules; spending on politics is free speech.

public_financing.t: Candidates who accept spending limits should get public money matching small donations several times over.
Candidates who accept limits should get a modest amount of public money.

congress_term_limits.t: Members of Congress should be limited to 12 years or less.
yes: Term limits of 12 years or less

congress_term_limits.t: Members of Congress should be limited to about 18 to 24 years.
No term limits for Congress; voters can remove members.

court_term_limits.t: Future Supreme Court justices should serve 18-year terms.
Future justices should serve fixed terms of about 25 years.
Keep life terms for Supreme Court justices.

ranked_choice.t: All elections should use ranked-choice voting.
Each state or city should decide on ranked-choice voting.
yes: Letting each place choose its voting method

statehood: This should become a state only if its residents vote for it: {case}.

voting_age.t: 17-year-olds should vote if they'll be 18 by the next general election.

noncitizen_local_voting.t: Legal permanent residents should vote in local elections like school board races.
Each city should decide whether green card holders vote locally.
Ban noncitizen voting in local elections everywhere.
